solution:
Every angle of a rectangle is a right angle, so a diagonal and two adjacent sides form a right-angled triangle.
By Pythagoras' theorem, diagonal \(= \sqrt{7^2 + 24^2} = \sqrt{49 + 576} = \sqrt{625} = 25\) cm.
Hence the length of the diagonal is 25 cm.

Let the side of the square be \(a\) cm. Adjacent sides of a square are perpendicular, so by Pythagoras' theorem the diagonal is \(\sqrt{a^2 + a^2} = a\sqrt{2}\).
So \(a\sqrt{2} = 13\), which gives \(a = \frac{13}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{13\sqrt{2}}{2} = 6.5\sqrt{2}\) cm.
Hence the side of the square is \(6.5\sqrt{2}\) cm.

Let the two adjacent sides be \(3x\) cm and \(4x\) cm.
Opposite sides of a parallelogram are congruent, so the perimeter is \(2(3x + 4x) = 14x\).
\(14x = 112\), so \(x = 8\).
So the adjacent sides are \(3 \times 8 = 24\) cm and \(4 \times 8 = 32\) cm.
Hence the four sides measure 24 cm, 32 cm, 24 cm and 32 cm.

The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular bisectors of each other. Let them meet at O.
So \(PO = \frac{1}{2} \times 20 = 10\) cm, \(QO = \frac{1}{2} \times 48 = 24\) cm and \(\angle POQ = 90^{\circ}\).
In right-angled \(\triangle\)POQ, by Pythagoras' theorem \(PQ = \sqrt{10^2 + 24^2} = \sqrt{100 + 576} = \sqrt{676} = 26\) cm.
Hence the length of side PQ is 26 cm.

In rectangle PQRS the diagonals PR and QS meet at M, and P-M-R and Q-M-S are straight lines.
So \(\angle PMS\) is vertically opposite \(\angle QMR\), giving \(\angle PMS = 50^{\circ}\).
The diagonals of a rectangle are congruent and bisect each other, so \(MP = MS\) and \(\triangle\)PMS is isosceles.
So \(\angle MPS = \angle MSP\), and \(\angle MPS + \angle MSP + \angle PMS = 180^{\circ}\).
So \(2\,\angle MPS = 180^{\circ} - 50^{\circ} = 130^{\circ}\), giving \(\angle MPS = 65^{\circ}\).
Hence \(\angle MPS = 65^{\circ}\).

In \(\square\)ABQP, seg AB \(\parallel\) seg PQ and seg AB \(\cong\) seg PQ (given).
By the test 'one pair of opposite sides parallel and congruent', \(\square\)ABQP is a parallelogram, so seg AP \(\parallel\) seg BQ and \(AP = BQ\).
In \(\square\)ACRP, seg AC \(\parallel\) seg PR and seg AC \(\cong\) seg PR (given).
By the same test \(\square\)ACRP is a parallelogram, so seg AP \(\parallel\) seg CR and \(AP = CR\).
So seg BQ \(\parallel\) seg CR (both are parallel to seg AP) and \(BQ = CR\) (both equal AP).
So in \(\square\)BQRC the opposite sides BQ and CR are parallel and congruent, and therefore \(\square\)BQRC is a parallelogram.
The remaining pair of opposite sides of a parallelogram is also parallel and congruent.
Hence seg BC \(\parallel\) seg QR and seg BC \(\cong\) seg QR.

Construction: join D and Q, and produce seg DQ to meet ray AB at point E.
In \(\triangle\)DCQ and \(\triangle\)EBQ: seg CQ \(\cong\) seg BQ (Q is the midpoint of seg BC), \(\angle DQC \cong \angle EQB\) (vertically opposite angles) and \(\angle DCQ \cong \angle EBQ\) (alternate angles, since DC \(\parallel\) AB with transversal BC).
So \(\triangle\)DCQ \(\cong\) \(\triangle\)EBQ by the ASA test.
So \(DQ = EQ\) and \(DC = BE\) (c.s.c.t.), which means Q is the midpoint of seg DE.
Now in \(\triangle\)ADE, P is the midpoint of side AD and Q is the midpoint of side DE.
By the midpoint theorem, seg PQ \(\parallel\) seg AE and \(PQ = \frac{1}{2}AE\).
Seg AE lies along line AB, so seg PQ \(\parallel\) AB, and \(AE = AB + BE = AB + DC\).
Hence PQ \(\parallel\) AB and \(PQ = \frac{1}{2}(AB + DC)\).

Construction: join D and M, and produce seg DM to meet side AB at point E.
In \(\triangle\)DCM and \(\triangle\)EAM: seg CM \(\cong\) seg AM (M is the midpoint of diagonal AC), \(\angle DMC \cong \angle EMA\) (vertically opposite angles) and \(\angle DCM \cong \angle EAM\) (alternate angles, since DC \(\parallel\) AB with transversal AC).
So \(\triangle\)DCM \(\cong\) \(\triangle\)EAM by the ASA test, giving \(DM = EM\).
So M is the midpoint of seg DE.
Now in \(\triangle\)DEB, M is the midpoint of side DE and N is the midpoint of side DB (N is the midpoint of diagonal DB).
By the midpoint theorem, seg MN \(\parallel\) seg EB.
Seg EB lies along side AB.
Hence MN \(\parallel\) AB.
